properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 4:16AM EDT until September 10 at 8:30AM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
FFWILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Adams County in south central Ohio...
Southern Pike County in south central Ohio...
Northern Scioto County in south central Ohio...

* Until 830 AM EDT.

* At 416 AM EDT, radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain
across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are
possible. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Peebles, Lucasville, Clarktown, Rarden, Otway, Mount Joy, Ladd,
Bear Creek, Wakefield, Poplar Grove, Smoky Corners, Locust Grove,
Germany, Serpent Mound, Stockdale, Minford and May Hill.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flash flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 10 at 6:40AM EDT until September 10 at 7:45AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...

* Until 745 AM EDT.

* At 639 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 9 nm south of T
Tower, moving west at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for severe thunderstorms with wind gusts in excess of 50
knots, extremely rough seas, frequent lightning, and torrential
downpours. Be advised that any severe thunderstorm can spawn a
waterspout or tornado. Stay low or go below, and make sure all on
board are wearing life jackets.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 10 at 5:50AM CDT until September 10 at 7:15AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 715 AM CDT.

* At 550 AM CDT, a cluster of severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts was located 20 nm east of Ship Shoal 198, or
23 nm south of Isle Derniers. The cluster of severe thunderstorms
were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels and oil rigs...and create suddenly higher waves.
Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The cluster of severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open
waters.
properties.instruction:
Strong winds will be dangerous for boaters or anyone near the water.
Boaters should avoid waterspouts and never try to navigate near them.
Make sure all on board are wearing life jackets. Seek shelter or move
to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in

County.

Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 affecting Manatee County.

recent heavy rainfall.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening to Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, River Drive and Squirrel Run Way downstream

will then fall below flood stage early Saturday morning.

feet on 08/26/1945.
